hook.text: We call them 'cavemen,' but most ice age humans didn't live deep in caves. They camped near the entrance.

buildup.text: Cave mouths offered natural shelter from wind and rain while keeping daylight and easy escape routes.

discovery.text: Deep caves were dark and damp—poor for living but perfect for rituals, art, and storage.

twist.text: Many ice age sites are open-air camps. Caves just preserve evidence better, biasing our picture.

climax.text: The 'caveman' label underestimates people who built huts, traveled far, and used caves strategically.

punchline.text: They weren't cave-dwellers. They were cave users.

quiz.question: How did ice age humans actually use caves?
options: Entrances for shelter; deep areas for art and ritual
